title: Unresolved questions in nudging research: Putting the psychology back in nudging
abstract: Abstract Nudging interventions are broadly defined as a rearrangement of a choice context that gently suggests a specific choice. Their increasing popularity has attracted attention and discussion from researchers, policy makers, and practitioners alike. After some applications to domains such as health, environmental issues, and retirement savings, the next step in nudging is to understand the psychological boundary conditions when applied to varied domains of daily life. It is yet unclear for example to what extent nudging interventions can be transparent without losing effectiveness, or how permanent the effects are. These unresolved questions may have contributed to heated political and scientific discussions, on for example the ethics of using nudges in the public health domain, due to the missing scientific evidence. Indeed, this popularity may have led to forget how nudging harnesses insights from decades of research in psychology to change people's behavior. The aim of this paper is to shift the focus back to the psychological premises nudges were built upon. It summarizes several outstanding questions that future research in the psychology of nudging should address. Advancing research in nudging will help to improve our understanding of applied nudging interventions and provide clarity to debates such as ethical appropriateness, effectiveness, and public approval.

claims.text: Nudging interventions are broadly defined as a rearrangement of a choice context that gently suggests a specific choice.
It is unclear to what extent nudging interventions can be transparent without losing effectiveness.
It is unclear how permanent the effects of nudging interventions are.
Nudging harnesses insights from research in psychology to change human behavior.

limitations.text: Missing scientific evidence regarding key questions like transparency and permanence has fueled contentious debates on the ethics of nudging.

future_work.text: Understand the psychological boundary conditions of nudging when applied across varied domains of daily life.
Determine the extent to which nudging interventions can remain transparent without losing effectiveness.
Investigate the temporal permanence and long-term effects of nudging interventions.
